name: Jupiter Skirmish (test)
about: A test of the planet backdrop: The Dogfight's fight, ship for ship, wave for wave and line for line (this file is dogfight.mission.json with a new id and name, a backdrop block and one more briefing stage), moved in front of Jupiter. The planet is drawn by the sky, 200,000 km from the viewer (its centre; 2.8 radii, 42 degrees across), so it has no parallax however far the fight drifts; the Sun is at 5.2 AU. No radio line here is new: every message is the Dogfight's, word for word, with the clips it already has. The map is Cassini's (NASA, public domain).

backdrop.bodyWhy: Sky/Resources/MonolithSky/Bodies/jupiter.body.json: Cassini's map of Jupiter, its pole, its winds, its Great Red Spot
backdrop.distanceKmWhy: from the viewer to the planet's centre: 2.8 radii, so the disc is 42 degrees across, three quarters of the cockpit's 55 degree frame height and half its width: it looms, and still fits whole when you look at it. 150,000 km (57 degrees) overflows the frame, 250,000 km (33 degrees) is a big moon, not a world
backdrop.directionWhy: ours: the Warden, three kilometres ahead of the player at the start, stands in front of the planet's upper limb; the planet's centre lies a little right of the opening heading and just below the horizon
backdrop.sunWhy: ours: the Sun behind the player's left shoulder, 123 degrees from the planet (phase angle 57): the disc is four fifths lit with its soft terminator down the right limb, and the ships, seen toward the planet, are lit from three quarters behind, so they carry shape against it. It is 6 degrees above the horizon plane because Jupiter's Sun is always within a few degrees of its equator (its axis is tilted 3 degrees): the same plane as its moons, so a moon in front of the Sun throws its shadow on the clouds. Jupiter orbits at 5.2 AU, where sunlight is 1/27 of Earth's

look.planetshineWhy: ours: the physical amount (Jupiter's reflected light is about 2 percent of the Sun's on a hull facing it) lands in the toe of the tonemapper and does not read; three times is a warm fill a viewer can see on the faces that turn to the planet, and still well below the Sun's key
look.ambientScaleWhy: ours: the sky's cold fill turned down to 30 percent, so the planet's warm light is the main fill on its side

backdrop.grsLongitudeWhy: ours: the Great Red Spot 22 degrees left of the disc's centre at the start, on the lit half; the planet's spin carries it right, toward the terminator, during the fight
backdrop.motionWhy: slow motion, ours, for reading (the body's own defaults, written here so the mission shows them): the planet turns 0.06 degree a second (real 0.01), the bands slide at 120 times their real winds, the Great Red Spot turns once in 12 minutes, the moons go round 100 times faster than real (Io once in 25 minutes, Europa once in 51)
backdrop.moonsWhy: ours: they start where their orbits (421,700 and 671,100 km from the planet's centre, in its equator plane) put them at these angles from the sunward point: Io 8 degrees left of the planet's limb, a seven pixel disc at 1080p, Europa 14 degrees right of it, four pixels. Io swings sunward and its shadow crosses the lit clouds from about 4 to 5.5 minutes into the fight; Europa goes behind the planet at about 9 minutes

arrivalCap.valueWhy: ours: at most this many of Earth's wave fighters alive at once per level (design section 7: a small cap per difficulty); the bombers and their escort come on top (their wings are not capped)

briefing.title: Jupiter Skirmish (test)
stages: Sable flight, you are the Small Mercy's screen. Earth's corvette, the Warden, holds three kilometres ahead: flak, guns, and two beam turrets forward on top.
Earth will send its drones in waves, from every side. With the third, a bomber wing comes for the Mercy.
(Test) The same fight as The Dogfight, in front of Jupiter.

questions.a: Keep the Mercy flying. Take the Warden apart. Stop the bombers.
Six waves of drones, three Censer bombers with two Vigil escorts, and the Warden's guns. Its beams are the ones that kill the Mercy.

debriefing.text: Warden's gone and the Mercy's still flying. Not bad, Sable.
We lost the Mercy. Sit with that. Then get some sleep.
None of the Censers went home.

ships.name: Small Mercy
ships.selfHealWhy: a capital ship does not mend: the diaspora's living tech is a fighter's (at a capital's size it would out-heal any beam)

capital.holdBeamsWhy: ours, FS2's beam-lock: the Mercy's beams stay quiet until the player has silenced the Warden's two beam turrets; then they come free and finish it

ships.name: Warden
ships.hullScaleWhy: ours: 40,000 of the Deimos' 80,000, so the player's two torpedoes, the heavy gun on its parts and the Mercy's beams can finish it inside the loop

capital.weaponsWhy: the model's two forward dorsal anti-fighter turrets are its beam cannons (FS2's Deimos carries two slash beams): destroy them and the Warden's beams go quiet

ships.name: Sable 2
ships.ammoWhy: ours: a wingman's rack is a Myrmidon's (4 heat-seekers, 2 lock-ons), not the player's test-everything load
ships.goalWhy: they start free to engage; cover me or form up from the quick menu puts them back on the player, and they go back to covering when an order is done

wings.name: Choir
wings.arrivalWhy: ours: Earth's waves jump in round the fight, from the flanks and behind as well as past the Warden, so the dogfight comes to the player and the Mercy

wings.name: Compline
wings.about: Earth's last guard (ours, FS2's wing waves): while the Warden lives a pair keeps coming once the six waves and the bombers are spent and no Earth fighter is near the player, each next pair fifteen seconds after the last is destroyed, jumping in 1.8 km off the player and going for it. Without it the fight ended in a long quiet whenever the Warden outlived the last wave. The hand-written dogfight's lastGuard (dogfight.json) is the same, step for step

ships.ammoWhy: ours: two torpedoes each (FS2's Artemis carries more); three bombers' worth is two thirds of the Mercy's hull if every one lands

messages.text: Sable flight, Warden's three klicks out. Keep the drones off us and we'll all get home.
We were once like you. We have ascended.
You return to us, and you will be ascended.
Disable your shields, and prepare for your ascension.
You remember Earth. Earth does not remember you.
You have no place here anymore.
This will all be over soon.
Bombers inbound on the Mercy. Somebody deal with them.
Mercy here. The Warden's charging beams at us. Its two beam turrets, forward, on top. Take them out.
Mercy here. Hull's going. Any time now.

events.name: Choir in
events.whenWhy: ours: a short breath before the first wave

events.name: Psalm in
events.whenWhy: FS2's campaign: most enemy wings arrive when the previous wing is 66% destroyed (design appendix, 'Slaying Ravana'); the delay is ours (FS2's relays come 6 to 18 s after)

events.name: Compline in
events.whenWhy: Earth's last guard: every wave in and the bombers sent, no Earth fighter within 2.5 km of the player (the pacing's quiet range) and the Warden still alive; the wing's own waves follow

events.name: Bombers in
events.whenWhy: the bomber wing comes twenty seconds after the third wave is called

events.name: Beams down
events.whenWhy: FS2's beam-free: with the Warden's beams gone the Mercy's own come off their lock

events.name: Autopilot
events.about: Only when the AI flies the player's ship (soaks, checks, captures): it plays the objective as a player would. The beam turrets first, whatever else is about (they are what kills the Mercy); the Warden's hull only when no Earth fighter is within 2.5 km of it, the Mercy or a wingman (it goes to their help), until Earth's last guard is called (then the Warden, whatever is about: killing it is what stops them); otherwise it fights.

events.name: Area clear
events.whenWhy: the Warden destroyed and every wave cleared, bombers and escort included
